 The Vietnamese national team receives good news ahead of the championship match against Kyrgyzstan.
 TPO - The Vietnamese national team moved up one place to 98th in the FIFA world rankings thanks to Mozambique's stumble in the African Cup of Nations qualifiers. This good news comes just as coach Kim Sang-sik's team is about to play their final match for the 2026 Casper Cup.
 Báo Tiền Phong • 17/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Following Vietnam's victory over Chinese Taipei and Mozambique's loss, we moved up one place in the FIFA rankings. The Vietnamese national team has just moved up one place to 98th in the FIFA rankings. This advancement comes just before the decisive match for the championship title of the Casper Cup 2026 international friendly tournament against Kyrgyzstan at 7:00 PM tonight (November 17th) at Thien Truong Stadium.
 Specifically, the convincing 2-0 victory against Chinese Taipei in their opening match on November 11th earned the Vietnamese team 2.35 points. This result increased the team's total accumulated points from 1,231.29 to 1,233.64. Although the increase is not very large due to the difference in ranking, the points still serve as a foundation for the team to improve its position during the FIFA Days in November.
 The turning point that propelled Vietnam from 99th to 98th place came from an unexpected slip-up by their immediate rivals. Mozambique lost to Ethiopia 0-1 in the African Cup of Nations qualifiers, resulting in a significant points deduction and a drop to 99th place. Thanks to this, coach Kim Sang-sik's team seized 98th place without even needing to play their second match.
 You may also like The match against Kyrgyzstan (ranked 103rd) on the evening of November 17th will directly determine Vietnam's final ranking in 2026. A victory would add approximately 4.68 points, bringing their total to 1,238.32, thus securing their current position. Furthermore, Vietnam could even climb to 97th in the world rankings if Guatemala suffers another defeat against Canada in the return leg of the CONCACAF Nations League. 
 FIFA has adjusted the latest rankings. Conversely, an unfavorable result against the Central Asian representative would result in Vietnam losing points and risking dropping to 98th place. Their closest rival, Tajikistan, could easily overtake them if they defeat host Thailand in the King's Cup final on the same day. Therefore, a draw or a win against Kyrgyzstan is a mandatory task for the team to maintain control of their own destiny.
 Regardless of how tonight's match unfolds, the Vietnamese team is guaranteed a place in the top 100 in the world by the end of 2026. The chasing teams, such as El Salvador and Luxembourg, are unlikely to accumulate points due to missed matches or consecutive defeats in Europe. Mozambique itself will also be unable to close the gap even if they win against Ethiopia in the return match.
 You may also like Looking at the broader Southeast Asian football landscape, the November training camp saw several notable changes in the rankings. Thailand consolidated its position as the region's number one team, rising to 91st in the world and having the opportunity to reach 90th if they win the King's Cup. Meanwhile, Indonesia maintained its 116th position due to not playing any matches, while Malaysia dropped two places to 135th after their 0-2 loss to China.
 According to the schedule, the World Football Federation (FIFA) will announce the official rankings tomorrow (November 18th) after all international matches have concluded. A victory against Kyrgyzstan tonight would not only help the Vietnamese team lift the championship trophy at home in Thien Truong Stadium, but also affirm the progress of the new players given the opportunity to play by coach Kim during the FIFA Days in November.
